text:
emma_cs: Quick share — I put together a short field guide for go-live handoffs focused on tenant safeguards (queueing / warm pools / streaming fallbacks) + renewal-risk signals. Link: https://redwood.internal/cs/field-guide-tenant-safeguard :wave:

raj_ops: Nice. Can you paste the minimal checklist we should run during the preflight call? :clipboard:

emma_cs: Sure — minimal preflight checklist (10–15 min):
• Confirm warm_pool >= 10 for initial traffic window.
• Run a 1k-sample batch emulation for typical prompts.
• Prefill top 50 user prefixes into prefix cache.
• Set prefill_ttl = 30m for first 24h.
• Ensure client exposes X-Client-Queue and idempotency-key.

Also the quick header snippet we use on client side:
```
POST /v1/generate
Headers:
  X-Client-Queue: tenant-<TENANT_ID>-tok-<HEX>
  X-Warmpool: 10
  X-Idempotency-Key: <UUID>
  Accept: text/event-stream
```

maria_cse: Love that. Add a short "session_hint" too so we can correlate stream restarts to the UI session. Example: `X-Session-Hint: session-42`

devon_sre: Fallback idea — prefer streaming, but if first-token latency > 800ms for 3 consecutive requests, flip to non-streaming/generate-and-serve-cached-summary path for that tenant until warm_pool recovers. Avoids noisy partial streams.

emma_cs: We use a simple onboarding risk enum in CS tickets: `0=ok`, `1=watch`, `2=high`. Heuristics: 3 warm_pool misses => watch; NPS <= 5 + 2 SLA breaches in 7d => high.

oliver_pm: For enablement cadence I recommend: Day 0 kickoff, Day 3 warmup check, Day 7 perf + cost review, Day 14 renewal-risk sync (and document decisions in the playbook card).

emma_cs: Quick feedback capture snippet — single-question webhook we use after activation:
```
{ "question": "Rate live quality (1-7)", "meta": { "latency_ms": "${p95_latency}", "tokens": "${tokens_sent}" }, "webhook": "https://hooks.redwood.internal/cs-feedback" }
```
Send this at 24h and 7d. Low scores auto-create a follow-up playbook task.

raj_ops: Monitoring rules to add to the tenant card:
• warmpool_miss_rate > 5% over 15m -> page oncall
• streaming_drop_rate > 2% over 10m -> create ticket + downgrade to non-stream for affected sessions
• client_queue_backpressure > 70% -> throttle and notify CSM

devon_sre: Pro tip: run a lightweight emulator that replays 70% of expected tail queries from prod for 30m prelaunch. Example runner (super short):
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do \n  curl -s -H \"X-Client-Queue: tenant-$TENANT\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\
    -d '{\"prompt\":\"sample prompt\"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &\ndone\nwait
```
This surfaces connection churn and warm_pool cold misses quickly.

maria_cse: Renewal hunting signals we surface to AMs: usage drop >30% vs baseline + increase in short errors (4xx/5xx) + CSAT decline. If all three, open a "pause & fix" workshop and prioritize warm pool + prefix prefill.

emma_cs: I'll import this into the shared runbooks repo and create a playbook template. @onboard-bot can you create a playbook card with tags [go-live, warmpool, streaming-fallback, renewal-risk]?

onboard-bot: Playbook card created: https://board.redwood.internal/play/9876 — tags: go-live, warmpool, streaming-fallback, renewal-risk :white_check_mark:

emma_cs: Thanks — I'll assign owners and drop a 15m sync for Day 3 checks. :calendar:
